newsitem.title: MEXICO: New airport for Mexico City on track -- government.
newsitem.headline: New airport for Mexico City on track -- government.

text.p: Plans for building a new airport for Mexico City are on track, deputy Transport Minister Aaron Dichter said on Tuesday, but there was no indication yet where it would be situated.

"In the case of Mexico City's international airport, different studies are in place to resolve the saturation problem," Dichter said during a ceremony outlining the Communication and Transport Ministry's 1997 goals.
Government officials have said Mexico City's Benito Juarez airport is expected to outgrow its site, once on the city's outskirts but now close to large residential areas.
The airport is unable to expand because it is enveloped by homes and businesses, and its two runways are too close together to allow simultaneous take-offs and landings.

Plans to construct a new airport, either supplanting or complementing the present site, have been waylaid by a fight between two competing states, Hidalgo and the State of Mexico, both eager to host the project.
Last month, a Mexican financial daily reported that plans for the airport's construction had been put off for 15 years, but SCT officials later said the new airport had not beend delayed.
Government officials had said a decision on the airport site was due by year-end 1996.
Private estimates place the cost of a new airport at about $30 billion.
